title: Tuberculosis (TB)
subtitle: A potentially serious infectious disease that mainly affects the lungs, caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacteria. It spreads through the air when infected people cough, sneeze, or speak.

sections.title: Symptoms
sections.intro: TB comes in two forms: latent TB (infection with no symptoms, not contagious) and active TB disease (symptoms present, contagious). Active TB must be treated promptly.
items: Persistent cough lasting 3 or more weeks
Coughing up blood or mucus
Chest pain when breathing or coughing
Unintentional weight loss
Fatigue and night sweats
Fever and chills

sections.title: Causes
sections.intro: TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, a slow-growing bacterium that can lay dormant in the body for years before becoming active.
items: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, gram-positive, acid-fast bacillus
Airborne transmission, spreads when infected person coughs or sneezes
Risk increases with prolonged close contact with active TB patient
HIV co-infection dramatically increases TB risk

sections.title: Prevention
items: BCG vaccination, recommended for infants in high-TB-burden countries
Complete the full course of TB treatment, prevents drug-resistant TB
Good ventilation in living and working spaces
Test and treat latent TB in high risk individuals
Wear N95 mask when caring for active TB patients
Healthcare workers should get regular TB screening

sections.title: Treatment
items: Standard 6-month DOTS regimen: Isoniazid, Rifampicin, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol
Never skip doses, leads to drug-resistant TB (MDR-TB)
Drug-resistant TB requires 18, 24 months of treatment
Directly Observed Therapy (DOTS) ensures treatment completion
Nutritional support improves outcomes
Isolation during first 2 weeks of active treatment

facts: ~10% of latent TB becomes active disease
MDR-TB is a growing global health threat
